maker: National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology (AIST)
name: AIST HRP-5P
summary: A 182 cm, 101 kg bipedal research humanoid built for heavy labour on construction sites, in aircraft plants and shipyards; it has autonomously installed gypsum boards at a simulated residential building site.

germany.statusNote: Research prototype of Japan's national institute AIST, offered for collaborative R&D use with industry and academia, not for sale. No German or EU sales route.

specs.label: Height
specs.quote: As a 182 cm, 101 kg humanoid robot, HRP-5P was built on HRP series technologies

specs.label: Weight
specs.quote: As a 182 cm, 101 kg humanoid robot, HRP-5P was built on HRP series technologies

specs.label: Degrees of freedom
specs.conditions: neck 2, waist 3, arms 8 each, legs 6 each, hands 2
specs.quote: HRP-5P has a body with a total of 37 degrees of freedom: two in its neck, three in its waist, eight in its arms, six in its legs, and two in its hands.

specs.label: Arm load, arm extended horizontally
specs.quote: Each arm of HRP-5P, extended horizontally, can bear a weight of 2.9 kg

specs.label: Board carried in demo
specs.conditions: approx., gypsum board carried with both arms
specs.quote: HRP-5P carrying an approx. 13 kg board

notes: Simple hands with one degree of freedom each (two in total).
2.9 kg is the load per arm held horizontally at full extension; in the demo the robot lifted and carried an approx. 13 kg gypsum board with both arms.
Head sensors re-measure the surroundings in 3D while walking, also when the carried board blocks the view.

images.alt: AIST HRP-5P humanoid robot, standing and carrying a gypsum board

evidence.task: Autonomous gypsum board installation: separate a board from a stack, lift it, carry it to the wall, stand it against the wall and screw it to the wall
evidence.note: Done at a simulated residential construction site set up by AIST, not on a real site.

sources.title: Development of a Humanoid Robot Prototype, HRP-5P, Capable of Heavy Labor

openQuestions: No newer status report on HRP-5P (later versions, site trials) was read.
Runtime and power supply are not stated in the press release.
